sections.title: The Economic Reality of GPU Hosting
sections.body: High-performance AI computing has a 'hidden tax'—the cost of inefficiency and corporate overhead. Global cloud giants charge between $2.00 and $4.50 per GPU-hour for enterprise training nodes. This price includes expensive real estate in Northern Virginia, high utility taxes in Europe, and 70% gross margins for the provider. Kenya AI Compute operates on a different logic. By leveraging $0.04/kWh energy and lean modular OPEX in a Special Economic Zone, we provide the same computational power for $0.70 to $1.00 per hour. For a startup training a 70B parameter model, this isn't just a small saving—it's the difference between 3 months of runway and 6 months. We are enabling a new class of AI companies that are built on efficiency, not just venture capital. Additional context: the project follows a clear rollout roadmap that aligns low-cost energy, infrastructure reliability, and flexible deployment models.
